title: Storage, crates and the storage tab
summary: Behind the shop floor Supermarket Simulator keeps a storage side: the game defines crates, crate sale items, storage sections and a storage tab, which is where stock waits before it reaches a shelf.
body: Storage is organised into sections with their own layout, and the interface gives storage its own tab rather than mixing it with the shop floor.
Crates are objects in their own right, and a crate can also be offered for sale, which is why the game distinguishes a crate from a crate sale item.
Because stock waits in storage, how you arrange it decides how long a refill takes.
What this entry does not tell you: crate capacities, storage limits or how much a crate is worth when sold. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: Storage is laid out in sections with a defined arrangement.
Storage has its own interface tab.
A crate is an object, and a crate can also be sold as an item.
The build ships the crates and vegetable crates the storage work uses, with a colour texture of their own.
A further crate piece is shipped at a lower level of detail.
The crates are modelled at several levels of detail, and a produce crate has a display slot of its own.
